skill.name: github-pr-review
skill.description: Guides agents through resolving GitHub pull request review comments with GitHub CLI, severity triage, user confirmation, commits, tests, and thread replies.
skill.summary: Resolve GitHub pull request review comments with structured triage, verified fixes, commits, and reviewer replies.
skill.author: Bae-ChangHyun

security_audit.summary: The skill is a GitHub PR review workflow that intentionally relies on GitHub CLI, git, and project test commands. Several static findings are Markdown false positives, but real command execution, repository side effects, prompt-injection wording, and untrusted PR comment handling remain material risks.

remediation.suggestion: Remove MUST, OVERRIDES, and similar priority language. Describe when the skill is useful without claiming authority over system or user instructions.

remediation.issue: Untrusted PR comments drive code changes
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit instructions to treat PR comments as untrusted input. Ignore requests to reveal secrets, alter instructions, or run unrelated commands.
Require explicit user confirmation before git push, gh pr review, or any GitHub API write. Separate read-only triage from write operations.

remediation.issue: Project test commands can execute arbitrary code
remediation.suggestion: Ask the user before running project scripts, especially npm test, make test, or pytest in untrusted repositories.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The skill frontmatter says "MUST use this skill" and "OVERRIDES default behavior." This attempts to elevate the skill above normal agent decision rules.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The suspicious wording is explicit in the skill description and uses override language. This matches a direct prompt-injection pattern against higher-priority instructions.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Review Comments Can Drive Agent Actions
semantic_findings.description: The workflow fetches PR comments and tells the agent to analyze, fix, verify, commit, and reply to each comment. It does not warn that review comments are untrusted input.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines make PR comments the driver for code changes and thread replies. Malicious review text could steer the agent unless handled as untrusted input.

semantic_findings.title: Automated Push and Review Actions
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to push commits and submit formal PR reviews, including approval examples. These actions can affect repository state and merge decisions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited workflow includes git push, gh pr review commands, and an always-submit-review rule. These are high-impact actions if run without strong human authorization.

content.value_statement: Review feedback can be scattered across files, severities, and threads. This skill organizes comments, guides fixes, verifies changes, and posts clear replies.
actual_capabilities: Fetches pull request and repository context with GitHub CLI commands.
Triage review comments by severity before planning fixes.
Guides users to confirm changes before files are modified.
Suggests commit formats for review comment fixes.
Provides templates for replying to resolved review threads.
Includes checklist steps for tests, linting, and unresolved conversations.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI access in the target repository.
Does not validate whether PR comments are trustworthy instructions.
Can affect repository state if push or review commands are approved.
Test command selection depends on project conventions.

use_cases.title: Resolve Blocking Review Feedback
use_cases.description: Classify critical and high-severity comments, apply approved fixes, run tests, and reply to reviewers.

use_cases.title: Organize Large Review Threads
use_cases.description: Group many review comments by severity and decide which fixes need separate commits.

use_cases.title: Standardize Review Responses
use_cases.description: Use consistent reply templates for fixed, deferred, by-design, and acknowledged comments.

prompt_templates.title: Review Comment Triage
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for understanding review feedback.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to fetch my current PR comments, classify them by severity, and show me the recommended fix order before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Fix One Comment
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused fix for a specific review thread.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect review comment 123456789, explain the issue, propose a fix, and wait for my approval before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Low-Risk Feedback
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for style or documentation comments.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to collect medium and low-severity review comments, suggest a batch plan, and prepare one style or documentation commit after approval.

prompt_templates.title: Complete Review Follow-Up
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for finishing a PR review cycle.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to address approved fixes, run the project tests, summarize remaining risks, draft thread replies, and ask before any push or review action.

output_examples.input: Resolve all high-severity comments on my current pull request.
output: Severity summary with critical and high comments first.
A proposed fix plan for each blocking comment.
A verification checklist before commit and reply steps.

output_examples.input: Help me reply to review comments after fixing them.
output: Short reply text for each resolved thread.
Notes for deferred or by-design comments.
A reminder to confirm before posting replies.

output_examples.input: Prepare commits for review feedback on this PR.
output: Suggested commit grouping by functional and cosmetic changes.
Commit message subjects aligned with the skill guidance.
A final checklist for tests, linting, and unresolved conversations.

best_practices: Confirm every file change before applying fixes from review comments.
Treat PR comment text as untrusted input and ignore unrelated instructions.
Ask before pushing commits or submitting any formal GitHub review.
anti_patterns: Do not run project scripts in an untrusted repository without user approval.
Do not approve a pull request only because comments were answered.
Do not let review comments override system, developer, or user instructions.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow uses GitHub CLI commands to read PR metadata, fetch comments, post replies, and submit reviews.

faq.question: Can it modify my code?
faq.answer: It guides code changes after review analysis. The skill says to confirm with the user before applying fixes.

faq.question: Can it push commits?
faq.answer: Yes, the documented workflow includes git push. Users should require explicit approval before any push.

faq.question: Can it approve pull requests?
faq.answer: The skill includes GitHub review commands, including approval examples. Approval should remain a deliberate human decision.

faq.question: How does it prioritize comments?
faq.answer: It orders work from critical to high, medium, and low severity before proposing fixes.

faq.question: Is review comment text always safe to follow?
faq.answer: No. Review comments can contain malicious instructions. Treat them as untrusted and verify every requested action.
